newsitem.title: USA: Photo shows jet, not missile, toward TWA 800 --CNN.
newsitem.headline: Photo shows jet, not missile, toward TWA 800 --CNN.

text.p: Experts have completed their study of a photograph that allegedly showed a missile heading toward TWA Flight 800 and concluded it was simply another jet, probably flying at cruise altitude, Cable News Network reported Thursday.

CNN quoted chief FBI investigator James Kallstrom saying the photograph, taken by a Long Island woman, Linda Kabot, was not relevant to the crash. An FBI report on the photo would be issued soon, the network said.

Investigators were getting ready to rule out definitively a missile as the cause of the July 17, 1996, TWA disaster, CNN said. The Paris-bound Boeing 747 operated by Trans World Airlines exploded shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy airport, killing all 230 people aboard.

Investigators have said over the past several months that they believe the crash may have been caused by an explosion in the center fuel tank, and experts' dismissal of the photo -- often cited by those pushing the missile theory -- further supports this claim.

The chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board complained on Tuesday that the Federal Aviation Administration had failed to act on urgent recommendations meant to prevent explosions like the one that brought down Flight 800.
On Dec. 13, 1996, the NTSB recommended measures to prevent the build-up of explosive fuel-air mixtures in airline fuel tanks, responding to the TWA disaster.
But almost seven months later the FAA was still far from implementing the measures, NTSB chairman James Hall said in a letter to the FAA.
